- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual reversion.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods — if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — if last 3–5 days show rising sentiment + price, add 0.5–1.5% to final forecast to capture tail momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs — if forecast peaks too early, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
